content.title: About
content.content: Jambolan (Syzygium cumini), also known as jamun, Java plum, or black plum, is a tropical fruit tree native to India and Southeast Asia. Its oval, glossy, dark purple-to-black berries have a sweet, tart, astringent flavor and stain the tongue and lips purple. Jambolan is eaten fresh and used in juices, jams, syrups, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The fruit turns the tongue and lips purple because of its anthocyanin pigments.
Jambolan is popular in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and across South and Southeast Asia, where it is a seasonal summer fruit.
The fruit has a single large seed, and the seeds are used in traditional practices.
The tree is long-lived and can grow very tall.
The fruit is often eaten with a pinch of salt or black salt to balance its astringency.

items.title: Contains anthocyanins
items.content: These plant pigments give jambolan its dark color and have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Provides vitamin C
items.content: Jambolan contains vitamin C, which supports the immune system and skin.

items.title: Provides iron and potassium
items.content: These minerals support oxygen transport and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Jambolan contributes fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Jambolan is relatively low in calories and refreshing.

items.title: Astringency
items.content: The tannins in jambolan can be astringent and may cause constipation or a dry mouth if eaten in large amounts.

items.title: Blood sugar medication
items.content: Jambolan, especially its seed and leaf extracts, may lower blood sugar. People taking diabetes medication should consult a healthcare professional before using concentrated products.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Jambolan allergy is uncommon but can occur.

items.title: Staining and seeds
items.content: The juice stains clothes and teeth, and the large seeds should not be swallowed in quantity or eaten by young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Jambolan can be washed and eaten fresh, sprinkled with a little salt, blended into juices and drinks, or cooked into jams, syrups, and desserts. Remove the large seed before eating. Eat ripe fruit, since unripe fruit is very astringent.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Jambolan is very perishable. Store it in the refrigerator and eat it within two to three days. Wash it just before eating. The pulp can be frozen for longer storage.
